recreation_brief: 1) Set slide background to white. 2) Create six confusion-matrix boxes with dark-red borders and light-pink header strips. Place four in a left vertical stack (Threshold=0.0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.4) and two in a center stack (Threshold=0.6, 0.7). 3) Inside each box, add a 2x2 grid headed 'Predicted as' with columns P and N, and a vertical 'Actual' label on the left. Fill the grids with the exact values: 0.0→[[5,0],[6,0]]; 0.6→[[3,1],[1,5]]; 0.1→[[5,0],[4,2]]; 0.7→[[3,2],[0,6]]; 0.3→[[5,0],[2,4]]; 0.4→[[4,1],[1,5]]. 4) Under each grid add the two computation lines exactly as written (e.g. TPR=5/(5+0)=1 and FPR=6/(6+0)=1). 5) Add a 'Best (FPR)' callout above the Threshold=0.7 box. 6) In the bottom-center, add a wide box reading 'ROC Curve for Same Model -different thresholds'. 7) On the right, draw a large square ROC plot: label y-axis 'TPR' and x-axis 'FPR', add light gridlines, draw a dashed diagonal from lower-left to upper-right, and plot red circles at the approximate points listed. Connect them with arrows and annotate points with '0.1', '0.3', '0.4', '0.6'. 8) Place a small yellow circle containing '34' at the plot's top-right. 9) At bottom-right, add a formulas box with 'TPR = TP/(TP+FN)' and 'FPR = FP/(FP+TN)' as stacked fractions, plus a small 2x2 legend grid with TP/FN/FP/TN; fill TP and TN cells light green. 10) Use sans-serif fonts, bold red headers, and keep all text verbatim.
